subject: ACME POC: Integration & Trial Plan - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME POC - post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Sofia,

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday — appreciate the time. Per our call, here’s a concise recap and proposal for the POC/trial so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and owners. Please confirm or flag anything I missed.

Summary of objectives
- Validate Redwood inference for ACME Search Assistant use case: intent detection, reranking, and streaming chat for multi-turn clarifications.
- Measure latency at 95th pct, token unit cost, and answer relevance against your evaluation set.

Proposed success criteria
1) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end < 400ms for single-turn queries at pilot throughput (50 qps).
2) Quality: Top-1 rerank MRR improvement >= 10% over baseline on your benchmark set.
3) Stability: less than 1% error rate (time-outs or API errors) over a 48-hour run.
4) Integration: SDK-based integration with streaming responses and tool-calling to your entity resolution service.

POC plan & timeline (target 4 weeks)
- Week 1 (Nov 22-26): Access + sandbox setup — Redwood test API key, SDK drop-in, sample routes.
- Week 2 (Nov 29-Dec 3): Integration & ingestion — connect your eval set, implement streaming endpoints, tool-calling for entity resolution.
- Week 3 (Dec 6-10): Run evaluation — load tests, quality evals, telemetry collection.
- Week 4 (Dec 13-17): Findings & recommendation — cost/latency tradeoffs, quantization suggestions, rollout plan.

Ownership
- ACME: provide eval dataset, provide access to entity resolution tool (or API spec), SOC/security reviewer.
- Redwood: SDK & example routes, streaming + tool-calling implementation support, weekly check-ins, monitoring dashboard.

Next steps (action items)
- Alex: confirm success criteria + any additional metrics you care about (e.g., per-category latency).
- Sofia: share eval dataset access and API spec for entity resolution by EOD Fri (Nov 20).
- Rishi / David: internal kickoff to create the SDK sample app and share sandbox credentials.

Attachments: draft MOP (acme_poc_mop_v1.pdf) and Redwood SDK integration guide attached.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for next Monday unless you prefer an alternate time.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME POC - post-demo recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and minor tweaks on success criteria:

- Latency: 95th < 400ms is good; can we also capture p50 and p99 in the dashboard? p99 is important for our SLA modeling.
- Quality: instead of absolute MRR, can we also track precision@1 and recall on our intent categories (we care about edge-case categories with low prevalence).
- Integration: the entity resolution service is behind an internal API; we can provide a test endpoint with token-based auth.

Deliverables from our side:
- Sofia will share a masked eval set and API spec by Friday.
- I will confirm expected traffic profile (burst vs steady) and any special categories to prioritize.

Also — one ask: can you confirm that your streaming SDK supports incremental tool calling hooks (i.e., the SDK can pause generation, call our entity resolver, and resume with tool output)? If not, please outline an alternative.

Appreciate it.

—Alex
Product Lead, Search Infrastructure | ACME Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME POC - Integration details & SDK behavior

Hi Alex / Sofia — quick technical reply to confirm capabilities and proposed implementation approach.

Short answers:
- Yes, Redwood SDK supports streaming responses with incremental tool-calling hooks. We provide a client-side handler that can intercept generation checkpoints, call external tools (your entity resolver), and then continue generation with the tool output injected via the tool-calling API.
- We’ll provide an example using the Node SDK and a Python equivalent.

Proposed integration plan (technical)
1) Sandbox access & auth
   - We’ll create a sandbox API key scoped to the POC and share it with your engineering team (expires in 90 days).
2) SDK sample app
   - Node SDK sample demonstrating: streaming chat endpoint, tool-calling flow to entity resolver, and a small reranking client that hits our embeddings + reranker routes. (file: redwood_sdk_integration_guide_v1.pdf)
3) API routes to use
   - POST /v1/chat/stream — streaming chat with tool-calls
   - POST /v1/embeddings — for embedding ingestion & similarity
   - POST /v1/rerank — batch reranking endpoint for candidate lists
4) Telemetry & metrics
   - We’ll push latency, token counts, and error rates to the dashboard. You’ll get p50/p95/p99 latency plus per-route token breakdowns.
5) Load profile recommendations
   - For initial tests at 50 qps, we recommend a single dedicated slot with autoscale to burst capacity. We’ll provide guidance on batching settings to balance latency/cost.

Itemized ask for your infra team
- Provide a test endpoint and credentials for the entity resolver.
- Share a masked eval set in CSV/JSONL with fields: query, gold_answer, candidates (optional).

I’ll attach the SDK guide and a minimal sample app. We can do a technical pair-programming session next Tuesday to wire up streaming tool calls.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME POC - Integration & Trial Plan - confirmation and next steps

Great — thanks for the quick confirmations, Alex. Recapping final agreed items and owners so we can kick off Monday: 

Agreed success criteria (final)
- Latency metrics: p50/p95/p99 captured; target p95 < 400ms for single-turn, with p99 tracked for SLA modeling.
- Quality metrics: precision@1, MRR, and recall per intent category; target is >=10% MRR lift vs baseline.
- Stability: <1% API error rate over a 48-hour run.

Owners & immediate tasks
- ACME (Alex / Sofia): provide masked eval set + entity resolver test endpoint + expected traffic profile by Fri Nov 20 (Sofia to share).
- Redwood (Rishi / David): provision sandbox API key, deliver SDK sample app and integration guide (attached), schedule technical pairing session for Tue Nov 24 at 10:00 AM PT.
- Marissa: coordinate weekly check-ins and billing/POC success criteria alignment with procurement.

Attachments: acme_poc_mop_v1.pdf, redwood_sdk_integration_guide_v1.pdf

If all good, I’ll send calendar invites for the Tue pairing and our weekly check-in cadence.

Thanks everyone — excited to get started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
